title: The source workbook states no version date and records no approval
source: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Sheet Read me, document control and change log; Status
description: Version 2 has four sheets (Obligations, By source, By process, Key) and no read-me sheet, no version line, no date cell, no status cell and no approval or sign-off row. Version 3 opens with the two header lines of Template and Rules R8.1 and carries the change-log row '3, 22 November 2026, D-RCV-60 microservice realignment, T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash'. The issue date of version 2 is written as the R9 placeholder because no sheet states one, and version 3 is issued as Draft.
evidence: Workbook properties record creation on 27 October 2026 and last modification on 29 October 2026, which are file properties and not a version date. Sheets Obligations, By source, By process and Key contain no version, date, status, approval or signature row; sheet Obligations row 3 is blank in version 2.
proposed: Record the issue date of version 2 and the approval of version 3 from the document register in the Read me sheet, and keep the draft status until that approval exists.

title: The obligations map names no service owner
source: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Sheet Obligations columns Controls, Owner and the new columns I Owner service and J Service basis
description: The 32 obligation rows name a business role as owner (Compliance, Legal, product heads, Head of NPA, write-off committee, Application owner and so on) and name no service. Version 3 adds one owner service per obligation in column I, derived from the controls in column F, and the basis in column J. No obligation, ID, number, date, control or business owner changes.
evidence: Sheet Obligations column Owner: 32 rows, each a role; no row names a service. Ownership Map v1 sheets Services, Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs give the owner per object; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the objects each of the 19 services owns; Controls Catalog v4 columns O and P give the owner service of each of the 44 controls.
proposed: Confirm the owner service of each of the 32 obligations with Compliance, Legal and the service owners, and keep the basis column as the record of the ruling.

title: The reporting and outbound leg of REG-15 and REG-27 is covered by no control
source: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2; Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Sheet Obligations rows REG-15 and REG-27, columns Controls and Service basis; sheet By service note
description: REG-15 asks for a report of repossessed vehicles and loss on sale in the BOT format, and the only control it names is CTL-38, owned by S5 rwb-asset. REG-27 asks that credit information be reported and corrected, and the only control it names is CTL-02, owned by P1 rwb-source-data. The reporting and outbound-file work sits in P9 rwb-reporting (measures, snapshots and regulatory reports; JOB-15 reporting extract) and in P2 rwb-integration (outbound items; slide 43 FileDelivered and FileFailed), and neither is named by a control in these two rows. Version 3 keeps the owner service a direct read of the Controls cell and records the reporting and outbound owner in the basis column, so neither service is counted as an owner in sheet By service.
evidence: Sheet Obligations rows REG-15 and REG-27 column Controls: CTL-38 and CTL-02 only. Controls Catalog v4 rows CTL-38 and CTL-02 (owner service S5 rwb-asset and P1 rwb-source-data). Architecture v5 slide 41: P9 owns measures, snapshots, steering dashboard and regulatory reports; P2 owns interface config, file runs and outbound items. Architecture v5 slide 44: JOB-15 reporting extract is rwb-reporting. Architecture v5 slide 43: FileDelivered and FileFailed are produced by rwb-integration. Ownership Map v1 table outbound_item is P2.
proposed: Add a control on P9 rwb-reporting for the BOT repossessed-vehicle and loss-on-sale report and for the credit-bureau correction file, or extend the Controls cells of REG-15 and REG-27 to name the P2 outbound item, and reissue the map.

title: The personal data breach notification of REG-25 has no owning service
source: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v4
section: Sheet Obligations row REG-25; Ownership Map v1 sheets Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs
description: REG-25 requires the regulator to be notified of a personal data breach within the required time. The only control the row names is CTL-37, partner and agency oversight, owned by S9 rwb-partner, so column I records S9. The Ownership Map has no incident, breach, notification or continuity object, endpoint, event, workflow or job, so no service is fixed for the breach process itself and none is assumed. The statutory clock runs from detection, which no object in the Ownership Map records.
evidence: Sheet Obligations row REG-25 column Controls: CTL-37. Controls Catalog v4 row CTL-37 (owner service S9 rwb-partner, L2 12.4 Govern partners, first in E6). Ownership Map v1 sheets Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs contain no incident, breach, notification or continuity row; the L2 process 16.6 Manage incidents and continuity appears in no service catalogue row of Architecture v5 slide 41.
proposed: Add the incident and breach process to the Ownership Map (an incident record and an event in P9 rwb-reporting or P4 rwb-access), add a control for the breach notification and its time limit, then reissue this map with the new owner service.

title: The map and the Controls Catalog disagree on which controls answer four obligations
source: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2; Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v4
section: Sheet Obligations column Controls, rows REG-11, REG-22, REG-27 and REG-32; Controls Catalog v4 sheet Controls column Obligations, rows CTL-43 and CTL-44
description: The map lists REG-11 with CTL-02 and CTL-25, REG-22 with CTL-09 and CTL-11, REG-27 with CTL-02, and REG-32 with CTL-06, CTL-09, CTL-10 and CTL-37. The Obligations column of the Controls Catalog v4 also names CTL-43 for REG-22 and REG-32 and CTL-44 for REG-11 and REG-27. Both extra controls are owned by P1 rwb-source-data, so the owner service in column I is unchanged for REG-11 and REG-27, where P1 is already named, and would gain P1 for REG-22 and REG-32 if the catalog is right. Version 3 keeps the Controls cells word for word and states the difference in the basis column, so the owner service stays a direct read of this document's own controls.
evidence: Sheet Obligations column Controls: REG-11 'CTL-02, CTL-25'; REG-22 'CTL-09, CTL-11'; REG-27 'CTL-02'; REG-32 'CTL-06, CTL-09, CTL-10, CTL-37'. Controls Catalog v4 sheet Controls column L: CTL-43 'REG-22, REG-32'; CTL-44 'REG-11, REG-27'. Controls Catalog v4 columns O and P: CTL-43 and CTL-44 are P1 rwb-source-data (ACE view contract, data dictionary).
proposed: Reconcile the two documents in one pass: either add CTL-43 and CTL-44 to the Controls cells of REG-11, REG-22, REG-27 and REG-32, or remove them from the Controls Catalog Obligations column, and record the ruling in the Change Register.

title: Two obligations rest on the conduct sample whose owner service is itself an assumption
source: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2; Recovery Workbench Controls Catalog v4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: Sheet Obligations rows REG-02 and REG-08, column Controls (CTL-39)
description: REG-02 and REG-08 are met only through CTL-39, the monthly conduct sample over contacts, notices and decisions. The owner service of CTL-39, P9 rwb-reporting, was itself derived in the Controls Catalog v4 because the Ownership Map has no conduct, QA sample or sample object (CG-B-CTRL-32-4). Version 3 records P9 for both rows and names the dependency, so a change to that ruling changes the owner service of REG-02 and REG-08 with it.
evidence: Sheet Obligations rows REG-02 and REG-08 column Controls: CTL-39 only. Controls Catalog v4 row CTL-39: owner service P9 rwb-reporting, performed by the Conduct and QA officer, first in E8. Controls Catalog v4 issue CG-B-CTRL-32-4 records that the Ownership Map has no conduct or sample object.
proposed: Confirm P9 rwb-reporting as owner of the conduct sample in the Ownership Map before E8; this map then follows without change.

title: An obligation states no release, wave or date
source: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1
section: Sheet Obligations, whole sheet; sheet By service columns D and E
description: Only the controls carry a first release (First in E1 to E8 in the Controls Catalog v4). An obligation has no release, no wave and no date, so the point at which it becomes fully evidenced can only be read from the first release of its controls and the wave of the service that owns them. Version 3 adds no wave column and invents no epic or date: the wave of each service is written inside the basis text of column J, and sheet By service states the wave of each service.
evidence: Sheet Obligations has eight columns in version 2, none of them a release, epic, wave or date. Template and Rules R5.6 gives the wave per business epic and R1 U7 makes every release date tentative; no date is written in the workbook, so no date is marked (tentative).
proposed: Add a first-in (business epic) column to the obligations once Compliance confirms the scope, and show the wave per obligation in the next version.

title: The Owner column and the new Owner service column can be read as one owner
source: Recovery Workbench Regulatory Requirements Map v2
section: Sheet Obligations column G Owner and column I Owner service
description: Column G is the business role accountable for the obligation. Column I is the service that holds the control evidence. For REG-03, REG-10, REG-13 and REG-31 the two are different in kind: the Partner and agency manager against S9 rwb-partner, the product heads against S2 rwb-treatment, the write-off committee against S7 rwb-writeoff with P7 rwb-decision, and the Head of NPA against S5 rwb-asset. Version 3 keeps both columns and states in the Read me that they are different dimensions, so neither is read as replacing the other.
evidence: Sheet Obligations column Owner: 32 business roles. Version 3 column I: services. Architecture v5 slide 41 assigns objects, not accountability, to each service; the business role remains the accountable owner in every row.
proposed: Confirm that both columns are wanted in the next version, and consider renaming column G to Business owner so the two are not read as alternatives.
